newsitem.title: USA: D&P supports triple-B rating for Colombia.
newsitem.headline: D&P supports triple-B rating for Colombia.

text.p: Duff & Phelps Credit Rating Co said Tuesday that Colombia's history of conservative economic policy, sound debt management strategy and good economic prospects support its triple-B credit rating.
In a report, D&P reiterated its triple-B rating which was originally assigned in December 1993.
Colombia has maintained sound economic and financial policies despite ongoing political and social problems, D&P said in the report.

Colombia's economic growth has averaged a steady 3.7 percent since 1980, the highest for any Latin American country. Prudent economic policies underpin Colombia's solid fundamentals, it said. Key structural reforms will foster sustainable economic growth, according to the report.
"DCR believes there is little risk that the democratic process in Colombia will succumb to any type of dictatorship, including military rule," said D&P analyst Andres O'Byrne.
"Even under the current adverse political circumstances in Colombia, the democratic institutions enjoy widespread support," he said in the report.
The country has diversified its export base and sustained good export growth rates, despite the peso's continuous real appreciation, he said.

Colombia's strong international reserve position reflects the ability of the economy to attract foreign investments to finance its current account deficits. Because the United States is Colombia's most important trading partner, Colombia faces insignificant exchange rate risk on its dollar- denominated debt, he said.

Economic emergency measures will attempt to improve the fiscal imbalance and contain increasing capital inflows. "DCR believes the measures undertaken are positive; however, more ambitious reforms need to be taken at the central government level," O'Byrne said.
